summary: Burn WebGPU matched the exact Python summed loss and exported all 8 declared LoRA gradients across 8,192 values with cosine similarity 0.9999999999998102.

guardrails.detail: The browser exported exactly 8 tensors and 8,192 values with the Python names and shapes.
The WebGPU summed loss was exactly equal to the Python oracle value.
The separate fresh dense CPU/WASM regression retained all 52 tensors and its prior parity.

findings.label: WebGPU adapter parity established
findings.description: The GPU browser backend reproduced the complete adapter-gradient contract and exact summed loss inside every gate.

findings.label: WebGPU elapsed time exceeded CPU/WASM in this proof
findings.description: The measured 21.650-second end-to-end time includes backend initialization and readback and was much slower than the 0.978-second CPU/WASM run on this host.

limitations: The elapsed comparison is one cold local run and is not a general CPU-versus-GPU benchmark.
This is a local parity run, not a coordinator assignment with leases, retries, or canonical adapter state.
The complete base remains browser-resident and no offload path is tested.
The synthetic T0 fixture does not establish useful adaptation quality.
